## AmortizationLedgerPostingContext

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Application.SecurityMaster.AmortizationLedgerPostingContext</code>. Kind: `record`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/SecurityMasterAmortizationLedgerBridge.cs:73](../../../../src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/SecurityMasterAmortizationLedgerBridge.cs#L73).

Position-level context for posting projected cash flows. The legacy OpenLots input interprets LedgerTaxLot.UnitCost as a market quote under QuoteConvention; cost-basis relief instead uses monetary cost per recorded quantity. These inputs must not be interchanged. Historical pool accrual uses AccrualHoldings, whose FaceValueLot owns the acquisition quote basis and booked factor. Day-count weighting comes from the same terms as the projected coupon, while typed holdings supply the actual daily interest face.

## ApprovedFieldEditCanonicalMergeHandler

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Application.SecurityMaster.ApprovedFieldEditCanonicalMergeHandler</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/ApprovedFieldEditCanonicalMergeHandler.cs:36](../../../../src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/ApprovedFieldEditCanonicalMergeHandler.cs#L36).

Published-revision side effect (Order = 5, runs before the projection rebuild): merges an approved assetSpecificTerms.* field edit into the CANONICAL security terms by emitting a complete economic-definition amendment through IGovernedPublicationAmender — the current definition plus the one typed field change — so replay stays correct and the approved correction reaches cash-flow projection, amortization, pricing, and NAV instead of living only in the override overlay. Paths outside the asset-terms namespace stay overlay annotations by design (the documented D2 rationale), as do CLEARs (withdrawing an override reveals the canonical value, so there is nothing to merge) and paths nested deeper than the shapes the workbench validates (top-level declared terms, the profileFields envelope, and one-level profileFields.* fields). Idempotent: the merged document is rebuilt from the CURRENT canonical terms on every run, so a retried publish whose merge already landed detects a no-op (the patched document equals the stored one) and skips the amendment instead of appending a duplicate event. A failure leaves the revision Approved and the publish retryable, per the handler seam&#x27;s contract. The amendment names operator-workbench as its source system, so the amend seam&#x27;s cross-source conflict detection records the vendor-versus-operator disagreement as usual; the handler then best-effort resolves those freshly opened workbench-challenger conflicts in favor of the operator value — the maker-checker approval that published this revision already adjudicated it, and leaving the conflict open would queue a second governance decision for a value a reviewer just decided. No-op in composition roots without a Security Master backend (no projection store).

```csharp
public sealed class ApprovedFieldEditCanonicalMergeHandler : ISecurityMasterRevisionPublishedHandler, ISecurityMasterCanonicalMergeOutcomeReporter
```

Fans out to every registered ICorporateActionProvider for mastered symbols, normalizes announcements, computes cross-provider consensus over full economic value keys, and records every distinct observation in the durable proposal inbox. Provider agreement is retained as evidence and never appends or approves accounting by itself. The legacy append path remains only for hosts/tests that have not registered durable operations.

## CorporateActionScopeFanOutGate

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Application.SecurityMaster.CorporateActions.CorporateActionScopeFanOutGate</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/CorporateActions/CorporateActionScopeFanOutGate.cs:98](../../../../src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/CorporateActions/CorporateActionScopeFanOutGate.cs#L98).

Default gate over IAuthoritativeScopeFanOutService. Two conditions must both hold before a decision is applied, and they are separate questions. First, the affected set must be known: a non-authoritative fan-out is a refusal, never an empty affected set. Second, the known set must be applicable in one command: the durable acceptance path opens exactly one case in one serializable transaction, so a fact reaching several scopes cannot be applied without leaving the remainder un-cased. Refusing the multi-scope case is what keeps &quot;apply the decision atomically&quot; true rather than aspirational; lifting it is store work, not endpoint work. A fact reaching a scope the caller does not own is refused for the same reason and one more: the caller may not decide on another tenant&#x27;s behalf, and telling them the scope exists would itself be a cross-tenant disclosure. The refusal states that the fan-out is not confined to the caller&#x27;s own scope without naming the others.

## GovernedTermAmendmentRequiredException

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Application.SecurityMaster.GovernedTermAmendmentRequiredException</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/GovernedTermAmendmentRequiredException.cs:13](../../../../src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/GovernedTermAmendmentRequiredException.cs#L13).

A direct (operator) term amendment refused because governed term amendments are required: SecurityMasterWorkbenchOptions.RequireGovernedTermAmendments is on, or the Institutional governance profile is in force. The edit must be staged through the governed workbench (Draft → Submitted → Approved → Published) instead. Raised by SecurityMasterService itself, so every in-process caller of ISecurityMasterService sees the same refusal the HTTP routes and the WPF editor show. The HTTP routes answer it with 403 and the shared GovernedTermAmendmentPolicy.RefusalTitle and GovernedTermAmendmentPolicy.RefusalDetail.

## IAffectedLedgerBookResolver

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Application.SecurityMaster.IAffectedLedgerBookResolver</code>. Kind: `interface`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/IAffectedLedgerBookResolver.cs:19](../../../../src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/IAffectedLedgerBookResolver.cs#L19).

Resolves the durable accounting ledger books a published Security Master revision could have touched, so the period-aware restatement resolver (Phase 3) can route each book by its accounting period lock status. This is the publish-time feed for SecurityMasterRevisionPublishedEvent.AffectedLedgerBookIds; without it the resolver is a no-op end-to-end (an empty affected-book set short-circuits to no restatement). Restatement protects durable accounting books — the only ledger surface that carries an accounting-period lock. Those books are keyed by fund profile, so a fund-scoped impact resolves to that fund&#x27;s books. When the impact reports no ledger exposure, or no durable ledger backend is configured, there is no locked book to protect and the affected set is empty.
